units: every entry in 'ratios' is a length in camera.json units (L_eff; metres = ratio x physics.json L_eff_m, CHANGELOG 2026-10-25T22:47Z) EXCEPT bob_radius, which is r / |P_ring - bob| = r / L_c (provenance for dynamics' L_c/r; the builder takes r from physics.json)
frame: world frame of CONTRACT.md: pivot P = origin, X image-right in the swing plane, Y away from camera, Z up
scale_note: L_c is model-conditioned (from the period, owned by dynamics). The builder reads it from params/physics.json at build time; never hard-coded.
camera_note: Camera FIXED to params/camera.json (sha256 b8f51e1de285563db20dbfc056ee6bac6bce6e46efa565a2f780df549d223bd3) via camera/project.py, per-frame drift included; ratios are lengths / L_eff (camera gauge, = physics L_c when camera.json was written). Pixel-read sizes scaled by K = 1.0764 (camera-of-record image scale at the pivot vs the 700.6 px/L used in v1). Not fitted, reported: P_ring and bob diagnostics in the fit file (bob centre lies |B-P_ring| = 1.05-1.07 L_eff from P_ring: the camera gauge L_eff is the bob arc radius about P_eff, 0.081 below P_ring).
superseded: v1 proportions from scene/measure/fit_joint.json (own joint-fit camera, f=2749 px at f120) are superseded by the camera of record

bob_radius.method: least-squares fit of a parametric box model with the camera FIXED to params/camera.json (camera/project.py load_camera(frame=n)) to 20/19 hand-read landmarks plus 30/31 base top-edge points (edge_points.py, line constraints) in frames 0 (t=0 s) and 120 (t=5 s) (scene/measure/fit_fixedcam.py); rms 0.69 sigma, point residual rms 5.2 px. Cross-check: direct pixel ratio frame 0, bob radius 56.5 px / |P - bob centre| 700.6 px = 0.0806 (circle fit to silhouette; P at wire exit (1087,124))
bob_radius.note: If params/physics.json declares a bob radius the builder uses that value and reports the difference.

wire_diameter.method: apparent dark-line width 2.5-4 px over |P-bob| ~700 px, frames 0/120, per-row profile (scratch wire.py); motion blur/defocus widen it so this is an upper-leaning estimate

pin_shaft_radius.method: pin shaft apparent diameter 31 px (frame 0, 4x zoom, v 88.8-120) / ~700 px per L_c at the pivot depth

pin_head_radius.method: VR-11 re-measure (frame 120, 8x zoom, camera of record dv/dz = 659.7 px per L_eff at P): head apparent diameter 37.5 px (frame 0: 38.75 px). ck002 rendered ~35 px. The reference pin is NOT 1.5-2x thicker; it looks heavier because its fat head starts right at the loop (short exposed shaft)

pin_tip_x.method: least-squares fit of a parametric box model with the camera FIXED to params/camera.json (camera/project.py load_camera(frame=n)) to 20/19 hand-read landmarks plus 30/31 base top-edge points (edge_points.py, line constraints) in frames 0 (t=0 s) and 120 (t=5 s) (scene/measure/fit_fixedcam.py); rms 0.69 sigma, point residual rms 5.2 px (pin_tip landmark)

pin_head_start_x.method: VR-11 (frame 120, 8x zoom): head shoulder at u~1075 vs P at u 1086.8, du/dx = 556.7 px per L_eff at P -> -0.0212; the wire loop wraps the head's left end. Previous value (v1-v3) 0.004:

pin_head_start_x_v1.method: head shoulder sits just +X of the wire loop (frame 0/120 4x zoom: loop at u 1074-1085, head from ~1086); placed so the loop (centred at x=0) bears on the shoulder

wire_loop_outer_radius_measured.method: VR-11 (frame 120, 8x zoom): loop ring outer height 45 px / 659.7 px per L_eff, concentric with the head, no gap; the wire twists into a short V below the ring (ring bottom ~4.5 px above P). Builder uses a TIGHT loop: centreline radius = pin_head_radius + wire_radius + 0.0005 (check: measured outer 0.0341 vs model 0.0313)

wire_loop_radius_v1.method: loop ring around the pin: apparent outer height 44 px (frame 0, 4x zoom, v 79-123) => centreline radius ~0.028 L_c

pin_axis_z_fit.method: least-squares fit of a parametric box model with the camera FIXED to params/camera.json (camera/project.py load_camera(frame=n)) to 20/19 hand-read landmarks plus 30/31 base top-edge points (edge_points.py, line constraints) in frames 0 (t=0 s) and 120 (t=5 s) (scene/measure/fit_fixedcam.py); rms 0.69 sigma, point residual rms 5.2 px (free parameter). SINCE v4 (VR-11) THE BUILDER USES THIS (arm centre = pin axis). Earlier note: the builder used the contact-derived pin_axis_z = 2*loop_radius - wire_radius - pin_shaft_radius (loop rests on top of the shaft, wire leaves the loop bottom at P) = 0.0347; agreement is a consistency check

base_corner_radius.method: rounding of the vertical corners seen at the back-right and front-left silhouettes (~15-25 px), frame 0/120

base_top_edge_radius.method: width of the rounded top-edge highlight band along the front edge (~12-20 px), frame 0/120

base_bottom_edge_radius.method: bottom edge slightly softened, in shadow

wood_edge_radius.method: post and arm edges softened (~3-5 px highlight), frame 0 2x zoom

eyelet_radius.method: VR-12: brass stem/eyelet where the wire enters the bob, apparent width 4-5 px (frames 0 and 120, 12x zoom) / 659.7 px per L_eff

eyelet_height.method: VR-12: the bright stem shows 8-12 px long but INSIDE the bob silhouette, ending at its top edge (frames 0/120, 12x zoom): seen ~6 deg from above, the pole projects ~6 px inside the outline, so the stem is short. A first try of 0.012 L_eff stuck out above the outline (v012 draft); 0.006 keeps it within

bolt_radius.method: steel cap on the post -X face at arm height, apparent height 30 px (frame 0)

bolt_protrusion.method: the dark cap shows at u~680-695, v~140-170 in frame 0, i.e. 0-15 px left of the post's front-left silhouette (u~694). Projecting candidate positions through the frame-0 fitted camera, a cap on the -X face at y=0 must reach ~0.08-0.1 L_c out of the face to be visible there (0.018 in v004 and 0.03 in v005 stayed hidden). Likely the end of a through-bolt; the AI reference may be inconsistent here

derived_absolute_m.note: stand = ratio x L_eff_m; bob radius ratio x L_c (provenance only)
